correctness.rationale: Conditioning on one fixed point leaves a uniform bijection between the remaining positions and values. Writing Spearman's squared displacement as an affine function of the rank inner product gives the exact conditional mean after one finite-population expectation. Summing the coordinate covariances uses a centered-square identity. The standard permutation covariance of centered ranks gives the exact null variance of rho, while two fixed-point inclusion probabilities give Var(F)=1. Exhaustive exact enumeration through n=9 independently checks every displayed mixed-moment identity.

value.rationale: Fixed points are exact rank agreements, while Spearman's rho is the canonical quadratic rank-displacement measure. The theorem quantifies exactly how an exact agreement at a specific rank affects global concordance: central matches can be neutral, endpoint matches have the strongest effect, and the entire location dependence is a simple parabola. The aggregate identity Cov(F,rho)=Var(rho) gives the unusually clean best linear predictor 1+rho for the number of exact rank matches under the null. This is a natural finite-sample calibration linking a local agreement count to a standard global rank statistic, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
